newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-HOLDERS INDEPENDIENTE FALL AT FIRST HURDLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS INDEPENDIENTE FALL AT FIRST HURDLE.

text.p: Holders Independiente were knocked out of the South American Supercup at the first hurdle when they were beaten 1-0 by Brazil's Flamengo on Wednesday.
The result in the second leg of their first round tie gave Flamengo a 1-0 aggregate win over the team who beat them in the final of last year's competition.
It was Independiente's first defeat under veteran coach Cesar Luis Menotti.

The Argentine championship leaders were knocked out by a 39th minute goal by midfielder Fabio Baiano but could have lost by a bigger margin if Flamengo's international striker Bebeto had been on target with any one of several chances.

Flamengo chose to play the match in Brasilia where they felt they could get a better crowd than in their home city of Rio de Janeiro. The club also say that the fees for using Rio's Maracana stadium are too expensive.
Boca Juniors beat Argentinos Juniors 3-0 in a all-Argentine clash despite fielding seven reserves.
Coach Carlos Bilardo chose to save most of his team for Sunday's Argentine championship clash with arch-rivals River Plate, who trail Independiente on goal difference.
Boca and Argentinos are in a three-team group that also includes Argentine side Racing Club. Boca and Racing meet in the decisive game next week with Boca needing a draw to go through.
Argentinos Juniors, relegated from the Argentine first division this season, have played all their games and have only one point to show for their efforts.
The Supercup is played every year between past winners of the Libertadores Cup.
